answer_1.quote: The overall goal is a single agent that can display all these skills. As some of the subtasks have very large datasets, e.g. 2.2 billion utterances, they can possibly help the agent with other skills too. We thus build a model capable of training and multi-tasking on all these sources.

answer_2.quote: For all tasks, we use the following metrics: perplexity (PPL), BLEU, ROUGE-1,-2 and -L and F1, and also pick the metric most used in the literature as that subtask's 'Score' to compare to existing work.

answer_4.quote: In addition to automatic metrics, we perform human evaluation on two of the tasks to assess the abilities of our All Tasks MT conversational agent: the knowledge grounding task Wizard of Wikipedia (WoW) and the image grounding task Image Chat. We follow the same evaluation protocols as in ; , comparing our method to the existing approaches referenced in Table . This involves collecting 100 human-bot conversations for WoW using crowdworkers, involving 8-10 turns each, across seen topics (seen in the training set) and unseen topics, and 500 image-based responses for Image Chat. A separate set of crowdworkers are then used to compare models pairwise following the ACUTE-Eval procedure of , where they are asked to choose which is 'the more engaging response' for Image Chat (1500 trials) and 'Who would you prefer to talk to for a long conversation?' for WoW (400 trials).
answer_4.guideline: Pairwise comparison using ACUTE-Eval: for Image Chat, choose 'the more engaging response'; for WoW, choose 'Who would you prefer to talk to for a long conversation?'
